verdict: Intel swung back to profit in the fourth quarter — $2.7 billion attributable to Intel on $15.4 billion of revenue — as PC chip sales jumped 33%, though a $1.1 billion one-off benefit flattered the result and the next quarter is guided to a loss.

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: diluted, attributable to Intel; non-GAAP EPS was $0.54

kpis.label: Gross margin
kpis.note: up 6.5 points YoY; non-GAAP gross margin was 48.8%

kpis.label: Adjusted free cash flow
kpis.note: Intel's non-GAAP measure; operating cash flow was $4.6B in the quarter

segments.name: Client Computing Group
segments.note: PC and client chips; up 33% YoY. Segment operating income was $2,888M, up from $524M a year ago.

segments.name: Data Center and AI
segments.note: Xeon server chips and AI data-center products; down 10% YoY. Segment operating income was $78M, versus $126M a year ago.

segments.name: Network and Edge
segments.note: Networking and edge-computing chips; down 24% YoY. Segment operating loss was $(12)M, versus $126M of income a year ago.

segments.name: Mobileye
segments.note: Self-driving technology; up 13% YoY. Segment operating income was $242M, versus $210M a year ago.

segments.name: Intel Foundry Services
segments.note: Intel's chip factories, shown at their $291M of sales to outside customers only (up 63% YoY). Foundry lost $113M in the quarter.

segments.name: All other
segments.note: Smaller businesses and unallocated items; down 42% YoY. Segment operating loss was $(498)M.

flow.revenueNote: Money from selling chips and foundry services to outside customers.
flow.costOfRevenueNote: What it cost to make and deliver those chips — factories, materials, and unused capacity.
flow.grossProfitNote: Revenue left after the direct cost of making the chips — 45.7% of revenue, up from 39.2% a year ago.

opex.name: Research and development
opex.note: Developing new CPUs, AI accelerators and process technology; down from $4,464M a year ago.

opex.name: Marketing, general and administrative
opex.note: Sales, marketing and back-office costs; down from $1,706M a year ago.

opex.name: Restructuring and other charges
opex.note: A $1,142M benefit, not a cost — developments in the VLSI litigation, an EC fine and a fee for ending the Tower deal; Intel excludes these from its non-GAAP results.

flow.operatingIncomeNote: $2.6B of operating income — $7.0B of gross profit minus $4.5B of operating expenses.
flow.otherIncomeNote: An $86M gain on equity investments plus $117M of interest and other income.
flow.taxNote: A $128M tax provision on $2,788M of pre-tax income, a 4.6% GAAP tax rate; Intel's non-GAAP tax rate is 13.0%.
flow.netIncomeNote: The bottom line: $2,660M of net income — $2,669M attributable to Intel after $(9)M attributable to non-controlling interests.

follow100Note: Rows are rounded to the nearest cent; All other is rounded down a touch (1.15 vs 1.16) and cost of revenue likewise (54.25 vs 54.26) so the rounded rows sum exactly to the rounded profit of $17.27 per $100.

takeaways.title: Back in profit
takeaways.text: Net income attributable to Intel was $2,669M versus a $(664)M loss a year ago, on revenue of $15,406M, up 10%. Gross margin widened to 45.7% from 39.2%, and GAAP EPS was $0.63 versus $(0.16) a year ago.

takeaways.title: PC chips did the heavy lifting
takeaways.text: Client Computing revenue jumped 33% to $8,844M and its operating income rose to $2,888M from $524M. Data Center and AI fell 10% to $3,985M and Network and Edge fell 24% to $1,471M, so the recovery was a PC story, not a data-center one.

takeaways.title: A one-off benefit, and a loss guided next
takeaways.text: The restructuring line was a $1,142M benefit — VLSI litigation developments, an EC fine and a fee for ending the Tower deal — which flattered operating income. Intel also stretched machinery lives in 2023, lifting gross margin by about $2.5B for the year, and guided Q1 2024 to $12.2–13.2B of revenue with GAAP EPS of $(0.25).

oneTimers: $1,142M benefit in restructuring and other charges — a negative charge in the quarter, driven by developments in the VLSI litigation, an EC-imposed fine and a fee for ending the Tower Semiconductor acquisition; excluded from non-GAAP results.
An $86M gain on equity investments, net, versus $186M a year ago — mark-to-market moves on Intel's investment portfolio rather than chip sales; excluded from non-GAAP results.
A $39M gain from divestiture — deferred consideration on the NAND sale to SK hynix; excluded from non-GAAP results.
otherDetail: Other income of $203M combines an $86M gain on equity investments, net with $117M of interest and other, net. Intel recorded a $128M tax provision on $2,788M of pre-tax income, a 4.6% GAAP tax rate; the non-GAAP tax rate is 13.0%. In January 2023 Intel extended the estimated useful life of certain production machinery and equipment from five to eight years, which it estimates cut 2023 depreciation by $4.2B and lifted gross margin by about $2.5B.
footerNote: Q1 2024 guidance: revenue $12.2–13.2B, GAAP EPS $(0.25), non-GAAP EPS $0.13.
